facts.t: California banned caste discrimination before India defined it
facts.d: In 2023 California became the first jurisdiction in the world to explicitly outlaw caste discrimination. India has extensive constitutional and statutory protection, but no single statutory definition of caste discrimination in employment of that kind.

Indra Sawhney fixed reservations at a 50% ceiling in 1992. The EWS quota upheld in Janhit Abhiyan (2022) sits outside that ceiling — which is precisely why the judgment was decided 3:2 and remains contested.

facts.t: 97% of OBC benefits went to a quarter of the sub-castes
facts.d: The Rohini Commission, reporting in 2023 after six years, found that a small fraction of OBC communities had captured almost all central OBC benefits. That finding underpins the sub-categorisation debate the Supreme Court permitted in Davinder Singh (2024).

bank.q: With reference to Indra Sawhney (1992), consider the following statements:
s: It upheld 27% reservation for OBCs in public employment.
It applied the creamy layer exclusion.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Indra Sawhney expressly barred reservation in promotions — which is why the 77th Amendment inserted Article 16(4A) to restore it for SCs and STs.

bank.q: Sub-classification within Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes was held permissible in:
o: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024)
bank.e: Davinder Singh (2024). Nagaraj and Jarnail Singh concern promotions; Janhit Abhiyan concerns the EWS quota.

bank.q: Match List I (constitutional amendment) with List II (what it enabled):
pairs: 3. Special provisions for SEBC/SC/ST advancement, via Article 15(4)
4. Reservation in promotions for SC/ST, via Article 16(4A)
bank.e: The First Amendment answered Champakam with Article 15(4); the 93rd answered Inamdar with Article 15(5); the 103rd created the EWS category; the 77th created Article 16(4A).

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct about the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?
o: It has the powers of a civil court while inquiring
It can direct the registration of an FIR
Governments must consult it on major policy affecting SCs
bank.e: Its powers are recommendatory. The Punjab and Haryana High Court held in 2025 that a State SC Commission cannot order FIR registration, and the Delhi High Court in 2024 held the NCSC cannot issue directions in the nature of a civil or criminal court.

bank.as: The NCSC has strong constitutional design but weak enforceability.
bank.rs: Article 338(8) gives it civil-court powers of inquiry but no power of injunction.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — a point settled in All India Indian Overseas Bank SC/ST Welfare Association (1996).

bank.q: The conditions of quantifiable data on backwardness, inadequacy of representation and administrative efficiency were laid down in:
bank.e: M. Nagaraj (2006). Jarnail Singh (2018) later removed the backwardness requirement for SCs and STs while retaining the other two.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about equality regimes in comparative perspective:
s: India follows a substantive, anti-subordination model that permits reservations.
The United States bars quotas and struck down race-conscious admissions in SFFA v. Harvard.
The United Kingdom permits quotas under the Equality Act 2010.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The UK permits positive action, which is time-limited and tie-break in nature, but not quotas.

bank.q: All of the following are cited as factors reinforcing caste EXCEPT:
o: Around 90% of marriages remain intra-caste, per IHDS-II
Caste-based vote mobilisation and ticket distribution
Around 50% of UPSC entrants come from reserved categories
Around 85% of manual scavengers are Dalits
bank.e: That statistic is cited as a sign of transformation — evidence of educational and occupational mobility — not as a factor reinforcing caste.

bank.q: André Béteille's distinction relevant to caste and class is between:
bank.e: Béteille distinguishes status hierarchy, which caste represents, from achievement hierarchy, which class represents. M. N. Srinivas supplies the vertical–horizontal mobility formulation.

bank.q: Arrange the following judgments in correct chronological order:
bank.e: Champakam Dorairajan (1951) → Indra Sawhney (1992) → M. Nagaraj (2006) → Janhit Abhiyan (2022).

bank.q: With reference to reservation in educational institutions, consider the following:
s: T.M.A. Pai and P.A. Inamdar held that reservations could not be imposed on private unaided institutions.
Janhit Abhiyan struck down the 103rd Amendment.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Janhit Abhiyan upheld the 103rd Amendment and the 10% EWS quota; it did not strike it down.

bank.as: Inter-faith marriages remain around 1% of all marriages in India.
bank.rs: The Special Marriage Act's 30-day public notice requirement exposes couples to harassment.
bank.e: Both are true, but the Reason is only one contributing factor among many — khap panchayats, anti-conversion laws and social stigma also operate — so it is not the correct explanation of the figure on its own.
